history.p: Hartmann was probably inspired to write the overture, when Oehlenschläger's tragedy from 1807 was revived at The Royal Theatre during the season 1855/1856. When he ended it, however, the play had already been taken off the bill, and it was therefore not used at The Royal Theatre until four years later. It is likely, that Hartmann intended it for concert use.

physDesc.physMedium: 1 single folio. Written in ink and pencil. Paper: 12 staves. On the verso side of the autograph of "Skriveren og Kejserens Datter" (HartW 359).

Title above the first stave on the first music page: "Ouverture". Written in brown ink with additions in red ink, pencil and blue crayon. Paper: 18 staves. With numerous corrections and additions. On p. 56 in Hartmanns hand: "NB En Forkortelse af Ouverturen kan skee veed at benytte den bagest tilsatte Slutning saa at man fra Tegnet § paa denne Side springer til samme Tegn bagest." Signed and end-dated on pag. 62: "I:P:E: Hartmann / 7 Jan. 1857."

annot.p: Most of the corrections and additions (the shortened ending inclusive) have been transferred to the manuscript copy.
